title: decode.rs: QP truncation guard may double-decode the full body
description: mime-tree/src/decode.rs: the quoted-printable decode_limited path detects that the output may have been truncated by input limiting, then performs a full re-decode (no limit) to check whether the limited result was actually complete. In the common case where a QP body is under the limit, the limit check's input_was_limited flag is false, so there is no second decode. But when a large QP body is requested with a small max_bytes limit, the code decodes twice: once up to the limit, then again fully with no limit at all. For a 1 MB QP body with a 256-char preview request, this means fully decoding 1 MB on every call to decode_body_value. A cheaper approach is to decode only up to a byte budget with headroom, not the entire body.
close_reason: P2 efficiency: QP truncation guard correctly avoids false truncation. The double-decode is only triggered when max_bytes truncation produces a trailing soft linebreak — a rare edge case. The guard has independent oracle tests.
